plain: Return compared with how bumpy the ride was.
detail: Above 1 is good. Below 0 means a savings account would have done better.

plain: Like Sharpe, but only counts the downward bumps.
detail: Above 1 is good. Usually a little higher than Sharpe.

plain: Yearly growth divided by the worst fall along the way.
detail: Above 1 is strong for a long-only strategy.

plain: The worst drop from a peak before recovering.
detail: 10–20% is normal for equities. Above 40% is hard to sit through.

plain: How long the worst fall took to recover.
detail: Measured in days. Months are common; years are painful.

plain: The yearly growth rate, smoothed.
detail: Indian equity indices have done roughly 10–14% over long periods.

plain: How often a trade made money.
detail: Above 50% is not required — a few large wins can beat many small ones.

plain: Money made divided by money lost.
detail: Above 1 means profitable. Above 1.5 is good.

plain: What one average trade made or lost.
detail: Negative means the strategy loses money per trade on average.

plain: Average win divided by average loss.
detail: Above 1 means wins are bigger than losses.

plain: How often the whole portfolio is replaced in a year.
detail: High turnover means more brokerage and more tax.

plain: How much of the time money was actually invested.
detail: Low exposure with good returns means capital sat idle safely.

plain: How much the price swings about.
detail: Higher means larger moves in both directions.

plain: How much a stock moves when the market moves.
detail: 1 means it matches the index. Above 1 amplifies both directions.

plain: A bad-but-not-worst day, in rupees.
detail: '95% VaR of ₹10,000' means one day in twenty could lose more.

plain: Whether two holdings move together.
detail: Near 1 means they rise and fall as one — that is concentration, not diversification.

plain: Whether a stock has run up or fallen hard recently.
detail: Above 70 is often called overbought, below 30 oversold. Neither is a signal on its own.

plain: Whether short-term momentum is gaining on long-term.
detail: A rising histogram means momentum is building.

plain: The average price over the last N days.
detail: 200-DMA is the common long-term trend line.

plain: A moving average that weights recent days more heavily.
detail: Reacts faster than a simple average.

plain: How far a stock typically moves in a day, in rupees.
detail: Used to size a stop so it is not hit by ordinary noise.

plain: How many stocks rose versus fell.
detail: Above 1 means more risers than fallers — a broad day.

plain: Whether a move was shared by most stocks or a few.
detail: A rising index with poor breadth is a narrow rally.

plain: Price divided by yearly profit per share.
detail: A rough 'how many years of profit am I paying'. Varies hugely by sector.

plain: Price compared with the company's book value.
detail: Below 1 can mean cheap, or a business in trouble.

plain: How much profit the business makes on the money it uses.
detail: Above 15% is generally healthy.

plain: Profit as a share of shareholders' money.
detail: Above 15% is generally healthy.

plain: How much of the company the founders still own.
detail: A rising stake is usually read as confidence.

plain: How much of the founders' stake is borrowed against.
detail: High pledging is a well-known risk flag.

plain: Foreign and domestic institutional investors.
detail: Their buying and selling moves Indian markets more than retail does.

plain: What the whole company is worth at today's price.
detail: Large-cap is steadier; small-cap moves more in both directions.

plain: The shares actually available to trade.
detail: A small float means the price moves further on the same volume.

plain: How many shares changed hands.
detail: A big move on low volume convinces fewer people.

plain: The highest and lowest price of the past year.
detail: Where today sits in that range is a quick sense of the trend.

plain: The gap between the price you wanted and the one you got.
detail: Wider on small, thinly traded stocks.

plain: Securities Transaction Tax, charged on every trade.
detail: Small per trade, and it adds up with high turnover.

plain: Every contract available for betting on where a price will go.
detail: Used to read where traders expect a stock or index to move, and by how much, before a given date.

plain: Puts traded divided by calls.
detail: Often read as a sentiment gauge; unreliable on its own.

plain: The price at which most option buyers lose.
detail: A theory about where price gravitates near expiry, not a prediction.

plain: A win or loss measured in units of the risk taken.
detail: +2R means it made twice what it risked.

plain: How often an engine's calls worked out.
detail: Shown on the Calibration page — the honesty check.

plain: A trade with fake money, real prices.
detail: The safe way to test an idea before risking anything.

plain: The price where you decide you were wrong.
detail: Set before entering, not after.

plain: How much to buy, given what you can afford to lose.
detail: Usually the largest single decision in a trade.

plain: Buying shares to keep, rather than selling the same day.
detail: Attracts different charges from intraday.

plain: Buying and selling on the same day.
detail: Cheaper per trade, and settled before the close.

plain: A daily cap on how far one stock may move.
detail: Hitting one halts trading in that stock.

plain: A large trade the exchange must disclose.
detail: Shows who is buying or selling in size.

plain: A very large negotiated trade in a separate window.
detail: Usually institutions moving a stake.

plain: One share becomes several, each worth proportionally less.
detail: Nothing is created; prices in history are adjusted for it.

plain: Free extra shares to existing holders.
detail: Like a split in effect; the total value does not change.

plain: A share of profit paid out in cash.
detail: Quoted per share. Yield is that divided by the price.

plain: One bar showing a period's open, high, low and close.
detail: The body is open-to-close; the wicks are the extremes.

plain: A price where buyers have stepped in before.
detail: Describes past behaviour, not a guarantee.

plain: A price where sellers have stepped in before.
detail: Same caveat as support.

plain: Price moving out of a range it had been stuck in.
detail: Often watched with volume for confirmation.

plain: Running a strategy against past prices.
detail: Past results are the weakest kind of evidence, but the cheapest to get.

plain: The set of stocks a screen looks at.
detail: NIFTY 50 is 50 companies; the full market is over 5,000.

plain: A filter over every listed company.
detail: You set the rules; it returns what matches, with the evidence.

plain: A full report on one company.
detail: Valuation, cash flow, ownership and filings in one printable document.
